/itinerary_variants/0/stops/1/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ (성산일출봉, 'Sunrise Peak')** is a **5,000-year-old Surtseyan-type hydrovolcanic tuff cone** — a rare landform created when an underwater basalt eruption broke the sea surface, the magma met seawater, and the resulting steam-explosive ash built a **182 m fortress-shaped crater** rim instead of a typical lava cone. The result is what UNESCO formally calls **'an exceptional example of an emergent Surtseyan-type volcanic edifice'**. The crater is **600 m wide × 90 m deep**, ringed by **99 jagged rim rocks** that local lore likens to a stone crown. Seongsan carries the **Triple UNESCO designation**: **World Natural Heritage (inscribed 2007-07-02)** as part of the **'Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes' property**, **Biosphere Reserve (2002)**, and **Global Geopark (2010-10)** — a stack matched only by Hallasan itself among Korean sites. **18 Imperial Japanese WWII caves** (kamikaze suicide-boat shelters, 1945) are tunneled into the seaward base. Trail: **0.8 km one-way, ~140 m elevation gain, 60 min round trip** on wide stone steps. **Haenyeo (해녀) demonstrations** run once daily at 14:00 (1 show/day) at the rocky cove below the cone — Jeju women divers (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage 2016) descend without scuba gear. Admission updated **April 2025**: **Adult ₩5,000 / Youth+Child ₩2,500 / Group adult ₩1,600**, free under 7 and over 65. The summit deck is also part of the **Yeongjusipgyeong (Jeju 10 Scenic Wonders) canon**, and remains Korea's premier **annual New Year sunrise pilgrimage** destination — 50,000+ visitors ascend before dawn on January 1, with municipal sunrise-festival programming since 1995. **Udo Island (우도, 'Cow Island')** — Korea's largest secondary volcanic island — is clearly visible 4 km offshore from the summit, accessible by **15-min ferry from Seongsan Port** (₩10,500 round-trip) for guests with extra time on a different itinerary.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/highlights.source_en: **2.1 km cape trail** (~30 min, only 14 m gain) — wheelchair/stroller-friendly stretches
**Bangdupo Lighthouse** — octagonal, **flashes every 4 sec**, atop Bulgeun Oreum red volcanic cone
**Hyeopja Yeondae Beacon Fire Station** — 4 m × 9 m Joseon yeondae, **Special Monument No. 23-2**
**Tadao Ando architecture** — Glass House restaurant + Yumin Art Gallery (Phoenix Island)

**FREE cape admission**; Yumin Art Gallery + Glass House separately ticketed
⟦G0⟧ **clearly visible 4 km north** from the cape tip — perfect Triple-UNESCO panorama backdrop

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **⟦G0⟧ adds an easy coastal-walk section after Seongsan.** The cape gives guests a different angle on eastern Jeju: sea cliffs, lighthouse views, open grassland, and contemporary architecture near the coastline. It is placed here because it is close to Seongsan and keeps the morning route efficient before lunch. The stop is scenic but flexible, so the guide can shorten or extend the walk depending on wind, weather, and cruise-day timing.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/2/descriptio.source_en: **⟦G1⟧ (섭지코지)** is a narrow volcanic cape on Jeju's east coast. In Jeju dialect, **koji** means a cape or headland, and the place is known for open sea views, a gentle coastal path, the white lighthouse, and the broad view back toward ⟦G0⟧. The walk is scenic without being a heavy hike, so it works well for cruise guests who want strong photos and fresh sea air without spending the whole day climbing. Depending on time, guests may also see the Glass House area and the Yumin Art Museum exterior, both associated with architect Tadao Ando. The visit is kept flexible because wind, rain, gallery hours, and group walking speed can affect how much of the cape is covered.

/itinerary_variants/0/stops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: **Lunch is placed near the middle of the east route** to keep the day efficient after Seongsan and ⟦G0⟧. Restaurants in the Seongsan, Seongeup, or Pyoseon area make it easier to continue toward the afternoon village stop without a long detour. The guide chooses a suitable local restaurant based on group size, opening conditions, and timing. This also creates a practical buffer if cruise immigration, traffic, or morning photos take longer than expected.
